items.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 4 at 9:48PM PDT until October 9 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding and dangerous rip currents
expected due to the combination of high tides and elevated
surf.

* WHERE...San Diego and Orange County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Moderate flooding of sea water is possibly over
some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas. Moderate beach
erosion is possible to likely.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Elevated surf of 3-6 feet on south and
southwest-beaches. High tides are expected to peak between 6.5
and 7.0 feet during the morning and evenings. There is a
moderate chance that an upgrade to Coastal Flood Advisory
and/or High Surf Advisory will be needed. These products will
likely need to be extended into the weekend.
items.instruction: Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

items.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued October 4 at 9:10PM PDT until October 8 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures ranging
from the mid 80s to mid 90s at the beaches to the upper 90s for the
inland coastal areas and warm nights with lows in the 70s.

* WHERE...Orange County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
items.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.
